Jasmine / Karthik — bumping this as high priority. Summary of action items from our private-deploy playbook I want executed in parallel: 

- Confirm conntrack table size and ephemeral port usage on the customer's firewall (conntrack -S; conntrack -L | wc -l). If table > 90% capacity, increase max and reduce timeout for ESTABLISHED to 60s as a temporary defense.
- Apply MSS clamp on the customer egress (set-mss 1360) to prevent fragmentation across the private link.
- Validate SG state: ensure outbound established connections are allowed for ephemeral ports 1024-65535 (we've seen SGs that only allow a narrow ephemeral range).
- If NAT port reuse is visible (many short-lived flows from same src:port), consider short-term source-NAT port randomization and increase nat table size.

I'll draft commands for their NetOps to run if we can't query the gateway directly. Vanessa — can you check whether any recent SG changes landed in the last 48h on the Redwood-side config for Riverton?

Subject: Re: Riverton private cutover - conntrack / MTU / SG handoff (resolution steps)

Team / Peter — root cause and mitigation summary below (short):

Root cause: During the cutover the customer's branch firewall and the Redwood edge had a mismatch in PMTU/MSS handling. Large uploads caused IP fragmentation which some path elements dropped. That caused many retransmits and a high volume of short-lived connections hitting the customer's conntrack table, exhausting ephemeral ports and triggering conntrack churn and premature entry aging. In addition, an overly restrictive SG on the Redwood side limited allowed ephemeral ranges which prevented some re-established flows from succeeding.

What we changed (applied 10:40-10:55):
- Requested Riverton NetOps apply MSS clamp to 1360 on their branch egress (confirmed by Peter).
- We temporarily increased conntrack max_table_entries on the firewall and reduced ESTABLISHED timeout to 60s to lower table pressure.
- Redwood config: widened SG allowed ephemeral range to 1024-65535 for the peer link and enabled a short-lived NAT port randomization policy on the edge to reduce port reuse collisions.

Validation checks we ran:
- Before/after conntrack size: 85k -> 21k (steady)
- Successful large upload tested (250KB) from branch: completed without fragmentation / TCP resets
- No 502/504s in edge logs for the test window 10:57-11:00

Attachments: conntrack-diff.txt (showing pre/post change counts), verification-trace.txt (traceroute + mtr with 1500/1400 sizes)

Next steps / follow-up:
- Peter: please monitor for 24h and confirm no recurring failures. If stable, we can revert temporary conntrack timeout back to site baseline during low-traffic window.
- Marissa/Vanessa: let's schedule a short RFC to bake the MSS clamp suggestion into the cutover runbook and include a pre-cutover conntrack capacity check.

If anyone needs the exact commands we ran, paste below and I'll drop them into the jira RFC.

-- Karthik
